methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: The study analyzes the Pearson Correlation Coefficient among the implementation benefits of ISO 50001, SDG scores, and the factors of the Network Readiness Index (NRI)

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Macro-level correlational study of ISO 50001 adoption outcomes versus SDG scores and Network Readiness Index pillars across seven countries. Presents no EnPI/EnB measurement model: the reported energy savings, cost savings and CO2 reductions are aggregate award-case outcomes used as Pearson-correlation variables, not a characterised energy performance indicator or baseline (no normalisation variables, no functional form, no baseline construction). ISO 50001 is treated only as a management-standard adoption context.

paper_type.evidence_quote: this study examines the pivotal role of the energy management system, ISO 50001, in fostering technological innovation and sustainable development initiatives in seven selected developing and developed countries

stage1.notes: Country-level Pearson correlation among ISO 50001 energy-management outcomes (energy/cost savings, CO2 reduction), SDG scores and NRI pillars for 7 countries. No EnPI/EnB model, baseline, or normalisation variables. Ineligible under the v2.3 threshold; Stage 2/3 skipped.
